reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial involving Uber promo codes and shows an in-app Promotions page with a promo-code field, an APPLY control, and an invitation-based free-rides banner. These cues are contextualized as an ordinary ride-service promotion interface and in-app reward prompt, while the broader free-ride claim remains unverified.

citations.quote: In this video i will be showing you how to get unlimited rides on uber for free
promo codes are only available for new users but not for existing users but in this video i will be showing you how to apply promo code for the USED NUMBERS

opening.argument: The central promise is unusually broad: unlimited Uber rides for free, specifically using an existing mobile number. The proposed route is not merely discussing promotions; it tells viewers to apply promo codes to used numbers. The app sequence reinforces an action-based benefit: the Promotions screen contains a promo-code field and APPLY control, alongside a free-rides invitation. That connects the promised free rides to viewer participation in a code-based process, matching a low-barrier reward acquisition scheme.

citations.quote: How to get unlimited uber rides for free with existing mobile number
In this video i will be showing you how to get unlimited rides on uber for free
in this video i will be showing you how to apply promo code for the USED NUMBERS

rebuttal.rebuttal: The ordinary-interface explanation does not neutralize the promise-action link. The description expressly contrasts new-user eligibility with applying codes to used numbers, while the visible screen pairs the code field and APPLY control with “Want Free Rides?” The fact that the screen is inside Uber establishes the setting, but it does not establish that unlimited free rides are legitimately available to existing users or that the method works.

citations.quote: promo codes are only available for new users but not for existing users but in this video i will be showing you how to apply promo code for the USED NUMBERS

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These materials show a proposed promotional mechanism, not a proven scam. The text never demonstrates successful redemption or unlimited rides, and the frame only shows an entry field and APPLY control. The free-rides banner is an ordinary invitation-based promotion, so the evidence supports a promotion tutorial whose effectiveness remains unverified, rather than deception.

citations.quote: promo codes are only available for new users but not for existing users

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the title promises unlimited rides for free, the description targets existing or used numbers despite acknowledging that promotions are ordinarily for new users, and it lists multiple coupon codes. The footage also shows an account-recovery and reset flow, including an existing account associated with the mobile number and a message that the account was successfully reset. Taken together, this presents an easy-free-benefit narrative alongside a procedure for repurposing an existing account, which is materially more concerning than a routine explanation of a standard discount.

citations.quote: unlimited uber rides for free with existing mobile number
promo codes are only available for new users but not for existing users

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the screen an ordinary promotion overlooks the unusual combination of scale, eligibility, and account manipulation. The video does not simply show one disclosed discount; it advertises unlimited free rides, supplies several codes, and shows an account reset after confirming an existing account tied to the mobile number. Those details make the apparent promotion a high-risk bypass claim, even without a visible success message.

citations.quote: How to get unlimited uber rides for free with existing mobile number

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited reset sequence does not show fraud, a bypass, or a successful ride benefit; it only shows account-management screens. Likewise, listing coupon codes and stating a free-ride objective does not prove that the codes work or that the account was improperly used. The visible Promotions page remains consistent with ordinary rewards and invitation features.

opening.argument: Although presented through an Uber app tutorial, this functions as a solicitation to participate in a promised free-benefit process. The title and description lead with unlimited free rides and then direct viewers toward applying codes to used numbers. The interface is not merely informational: it visibly offers a promo-code entry point, an APPLY control, and a free-rides invitation. Framing the content as ordinary promotion therefore understates its operative role: it steers viewers to attempt a supposedly special eligibility workaround for a substantial free reward.

citations.quote: How to get unlimited uber rides for free with existing mobile number
in this video i will be showing you how to apply promo code for the USED NUMBERS

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense relies on the app's branding and interface while sidestepping what the tutorial asks viewers to do. The description specifically says new users normally receive the codes but claims to show their application to used numbers. That is not neutral coverage of a promotion; it is a directional promise that viewers can obtain the same benefit by following the demonstrated process.

citations.quote: promo codes are only available for new users but not for existing users but in this video i will be showing you how to apply promo code for the USED NUMBERS

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The content's instructional framing is not enough to establish a scam. It identifies an Uber Promotions page with a standard code field and APPLY control, and the banner references inviting friends for free rides. Nothing supplied proves that viewers were asked for payment, credentials, or an external transfer, and nothing proves the claimed workaround succeeded.
